{
  "edges": [
    {
      "fromKey": "n-1myxjth",
      "toKey": "n-1qw8yiu",
      "type": "caused",
      "rationale": "Upstream pressure stability (6.9 bar) combined with a downstream drop at the receiving header implies an interruption within the distribution system or service routing rather than upstream source failure, supporting the hypothesis of a localized event causing the reported air-low indication.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": [
        "fcd254db-75b3-4a9d-abec-44c5b6a9b34e#1"
      ],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If upstream pressure had dropped simultaneously, the cause would be source-side; if downstream valves were closed intentionally without record, it could explain localized loss.",
      "competingExplanation": "An unrecorded valve closure or service-routing change at a distribution point between P-U and H-R caused the drop while leaving upstream stable.",
      "evidenceGap": "No direct evidence of which specific valve(s) changed state; no record confirms whether an unauthorized line opening occurred during maintenance preparation."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-1cs3s92",
      "toKey": "n-1rww984",
      "type": "enabled",
      "rationale": "The absence of detailed field-operation logging and lack of documented confirmation for response steps created an environment where the point of interruption remained unidentified, delaying root cause assessment.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": [
        "24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1"
      ],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If desk entries had logged valve states and response confirmations, the interruption point could have been identified faster.",
      "competingExplanation": "The delay may also stem from communication breakdown rather than record limitations alone; both factors likely contributed.",
      "evidenceGap": "No direct evidence quantifying how much time was lost due to missing records versus miscommunication."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-1lq9li6",
      "toKey": "n-1qw8yiu",
      "type": "enabled",
      "rationale": "The area directory's inability to establish valve positions or pressure availability at any given time meant that the Utilities team could not verify whether a line opening had occurred, contributing to confusion during maintenance preparation.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": [
        "b678a928-a8d2-472d-bc03-2e1a3dc411e6#1"
      ],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If the directory had included real-time valve states, the team could have confirmed whether a line opening was authorized.",
      "competingExplanation": "Even with accurate records, human error or misinterpretation of procedures might still lead to confusion; however, lack of data is a primary enabler here.",
      "evidenceGap": "No evidence that alternative methods (manual checks) were attempted before relying on the directory."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-2jmrrk",
      "toKey": "n-1qw8yiu",
      "type": "enabled",
      "rationale": "The pending maintenance acceptance signature indicated that formal authorization for work had not been completed, increasing the risk of uncoordinated actions or misaligned expectations between Utilities and RHOB.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": [
        "eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1"
      ],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If the maintenance acceptance had been signed prior to work initiation, clear boundaries and responsibilities would have reduced ambiguity.",
      "competingExplanation": "Even with a signed form, miscommunication could still occur; however, unsigned forms increase systemic risk significantly.",
      "evidenceGap": "No evidence of whether informal verbal agreements were made instead of formal documentation."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-16kxawb",
      "toKey": "n-1qw8yiu",
      "type": "enabled",
      "rationale": "The lack of authorized line opening at the time of interruption suggests that either an unauthorized action occurred or a legitimate need was not properly communicated, creating conditions for unexpected pressure loss.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": [
        "24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1"
      ],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If a line opening had been authorized and documented, the interruption would have been expected and manageable.",
      "competingExplanation": "An unauthorized action by an individual without proper authorization could explain the event; however, no direct evidence supports this yet.",
      "evidenceGap": "No record of whether any informal requests or approvals were made outside formal channels."
    },
    {
      "fromKey": "n-1rww984",
      "toKey": "n-1qw8yiu",
      "type": "enabled",
      "rationale": "The absence of documented confirmation for response steps meant that the Utilities team may not have fully understood their role or responsibilities during the incident, leading to delays in addressing the issue.",
      "status": "supported",
      "sourceIds": [
        "24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1"
      ],
      "claimIds": [],
      "counterfactual": "If response steps had been documented and confirmed, the team could have acted more decisively upon receiving the alarm.",
      "competingExplanation": "Even with documentation, human factors like fatigue or distraction might still impair performance; however, lack of clarity exacerbates these risks.",
      "evidenceGap": "No evidence of whether similar incidents occurred previously due to undocumented procedures."
    }
  ],
  "decision": {
    "summary": "The analysis identifies multiple contributing conditions that enabled the instrument-air interruption: upstream stability combined with downstream drop suggests a localized distribution issue; lack of detailed logging and confirmation for response steps delayed root cause identification; inability of area directory to track valve states created ambiguity; pending maintenance acceptance increased systemic risk; unauthorized line opening or miscommunication contributed directly. Competing explanations include unrecorded service-routing changes versus human error, but evidence gaps prevent definitive conclusions.",
    "evidenceUsed": [
      "fcd254db-75b3-4a9d-abec-44c5b6a9b34e#1",
      "24ec1587-92e9-4320-82c2-30368d834f1d#1",
      "eaee59fe-70f4-4876-a21d-780814412078#1"
    ],
    "unknowns": [
      "Specific valve states during the event window.",
      "Whether informal verbal agreements replaced formal documentation."
    ],
    "alternatives": [
      "Unrecorded service-routing change vs. human error in operating procedures."
    ],
    "confidence": 0.75
  },"evidenceRequests":[

]
}
